literal: Critics on both sides reproached them.
idiomatic: Observers reproached them both.

literal: Before long he was reduced from prince and restored to his former noble rank.
idiomatic: Before long he was reduced from princely rank and restored to his former title.

literal: In the first year of Putai he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Government, and Inspector of Qingzhou, with overall command added.
idiomatic: In the first year of Putai he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Government, and Inspector of Qingzhou with overall command.

literal: Before he set out he died; posthumously made Grand General, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Guardian, posthumous title Wenxian.
idiomatic: He died before setting out and was posthumously made Grand General, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Guardian with the posthumous title Wenxian.

literal: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue, inherited the fief and held Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
idiomatic: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue, inherited the fief and served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

literal: Pingguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
idiomatic: Pingguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.

literal: Zhengguo's son Pingcheng died young.
idiomatic: Zhengguo's son Pingcheng died young.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made Commandant of the Horse Guards and given a posthumous marriage with the princess.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made Commandant of the Horse Guards and given a posthumous marriage with her.

literal: Shou's younger brother Duohou was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changning and held Supervisor of the Palace Guards.
idiomatic: Shou's younger brother Duohou was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changning and served as Supervisor of the Palace Guards.

literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yi Hun monopolized power and summoned Minister of Works Lu Li.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yi Hun seized power and summoned Minister of Works Lu Li.

literal: Li was then at a hot spring treating illness; Duohou told him: "Hun has a heart that disowns his lord.
idiomatic: Li was then taking the waters for illness; Duohou told him, "Hun harbors treason against his sovereign."

literal: Your Highness is what the masses look to; if you go you will surely be in peril.
idiomatic: "Your Highness is whom the realm looks to; if you go you will surely be in peril."

literal: You should return slowly and plot against him.
idiomatic: "Return slowly and plot against him."

literal: Li did not follow and was thereupon killed by Hun.
idiomatic: Li did not listen and was killed by Hun.

literal: Duohou was also killed.
idiomatic: Duohou was killed as well.

literal: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and Prince of Xihai.
idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and Prince of Xihai.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Long'er inherited the fief and was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: His son Long'er inherited the fief and was reduced to duke.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Bi had style and presence, knew how to place himself, ranged through the classics and histories, and was famed with Changsun Chengye, Lu Xidao, and others.
idiomatic: His son Bi had style and presence, knew his place, ranged through the classics and histories, and stood equal in renown with Changsun Chengye, Lu Xidao, and others.

literal: Yet he prized himself and looked down on others, and lost ground by this.
idiomatic: Yet he prized himself and looked down on others, and suffered for it.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen fixed the clans, he wished to make Bi Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy; Bi declined, saying it would be demeaning.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen fixed the clans he wished to make Bi Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy; Bi declined as beneath his station.

literal: The emperor said: "I wish to encourage and exhort the sons of the nobility; I humble you to go first.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I wish to encourage the sons of the nobility; I humble you to go first."

literal: White jade cast in mud—how can it be stained!
idiomatic: "White jade cast in mud cannot be stained!"

literal: Bi said: "Having met a bright age, I would be ashamed to sink in the mire.
idiomatic: Bi said, "In a bright age I would be ashamed to sink in the mire."

literal: It happened that Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered.
idiomatic: Just then Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered.

literal: The emperor said: "I make you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I appoint you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk."

literal: He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to him.
idiomatic: He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to the prince.

literal: Thus he came to the emperor's notice.
idiomatic: Thus he came to the emperor's notice.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was Director of the Household of Prince of Guangping Huai and often had the benefit of corrective admonition.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was Director of the Household of Prince of Guangping Huai and often offered useful corrective counsel.

literal: He was made Palace Secretariat Attendant and died as Inspector of Huazhou, posthumous title Yi.
idiomatic: He was made Palace Secretariat Attendant and died as Inspector of Huazhou with the posthumous title Yi.

literal: Han's younger brother Yan had talent and strength.
idiomatic: Han's younger brother Yan had talent and strength.

literal: As Attendant Cavalry he followed Emperor Taiwu in the campaign against Helian Chang.
idiomatic: As Attendant Cavalry he followed Emperor Taiwu against Helian Chang.

literal: His courage led the age; he was given the fief of Marquis of Niyang and appointed Supervisor of the Palace Guards.
idiomatic: His courage led the age; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Niyang and made Supervisor of the Palace Guards.

literal: Later he followed Emperor Taiwu from Mount Guo; a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled and captured it.
idiomatic: Later, following Emperor Taiwu from Mount Guo, a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled it down.

literal: The emperor sighed: "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses it!
idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses even that!"

literal: Later he followed campaigns against Bailong and in punitive expeditions against the Rouran; for merit his rank was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.
idiomatic: He later campaigned at Bailong and against the Rouran and, for merit, was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.

literal: Later he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and went out to garrison Liangzhou.
idiomatic: He was later made Director of the Palace Secretariat and sent to garrison Liangzhou.

literal: On his return he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Director of the Imperial Granary.
idiomatic: On his return he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrent Director of the Imperial Granary.

literal: Under Emperor Wencheng he was General Who Pacifies the West and supervised all armies in the western expedition against Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng he was General Who Pacifies the West and commanded the western expedition against Tuyuhun.

literal: Because in striking the enemy he did not advance, he was stripped of office and rank and banished to the frontier.
idiomatic: Because he failed to press the attack, he was stripped of office and rank and banished to the frontier.

literal: Emperor Wencheng, because Yan had shown merit in the former dynasty, summoned him as Grand Inner Custodian.
idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng, remembering Yan's merit under the former emperor, recalled him as Grand Inner Custodian.

literal: He died; posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Prince of Jian'an, posthumous title Kang.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West and Prince of Jian'an with the posthumous title Kang.

literal: His son Jisheng inherited.
idiomatic: His son Jisheng inherited.

literal: A clansman of Chong, Choushan, at the beginning of Emperor Daowu led his division to submit and, with Chong, joined hearts and shared strength to defend left and right.
idiomatic: Chong's clansman Choushan, at the beginning of Emperor Daowu, led his division to submit and, with Chong, fought side by side in defense of the throne.

literal: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and dwelt in the Eastern Barbarian quarter.
idiomatic: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and dwelt in the eastern quarter.

literal: His son Moti followed in pacifying the Central Plains and held Inspector of Xiangzhou and Acting Marquis of Lingyang.
idiomatic: His son Moti followed in pacifying the Central Plains and held Inspector of Xiangzhou with acting rank as Marquis of Lingyang.

literal: His descendants' offices were also illustrious.
idiomatic: His descendants likewise rose to illustrious office.

literal: Xi Jin was a man of Dai; his family for generations managed the imperial horse herds.
idiomatic: Xi Jin was a man of Dai; his family had for generations managed the imperial horse herds.

literal: His father Dan.
idiomatic: His father was Dan.

literal: He had favor with Emperor Zhaocheng.
idiomatic: He enjoyed favor under Emperor Zhaocheng.

literal: At that time the state had a fine horse called Zouliu; one night it suddenly bolted.
idiomatic: At that time the state owned a fine horse called Zouliu; one night it suddenly bolted.

literal: Later it was learned that the Southern Division Grandee Liu Kuren had stolen it and kept it in a cave dwelling.
idiomatic: It was later learned that Southern Division Grandee Liu Kuren had stolen it and hidden it in a cave dwelling.

literal: Dan heard and galloped to take the horse; Kuren, as the emperor's nephew-in-law relying on favor, was ashamed and turned to strike Dan; Dan seized his hair and tore it out, wounding one nipple.
idiomatic: Dan heard and galloped to reclaim the horse; Kuren, the emperor's nephew-in-law relying on favor, struck back in shame; Dan seized his hair and tore it out, wounding one nipple.

literal: When Fu Jian sent Kuren and Wei Chen to divide and lead the state's tribes, Dan was afraid and fled to Wei Chen.
idiomatic: When Fu Jian sent Kuren and Wei Chen to divide leadership of the tribes, Dan fled in fear to Wei Chen.

literal: When Emperor Daowu destroyed Wei Chen, Dan only then was able to return, and therefore his name and rank came after the old ministers.
idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu destroyed Wei Chen, Dan returned only late, and therefore his rank fell behind the old ministers.

literal: Jin was quick-witted and had judgment.
idiomatic: Jin was quick-witted and discerning.

literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Changsun Fei and others, together commanded the forbidden troops.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he, with Changsun Fei and others, jointly commanded the forbidden troops.

literal: Later he was made Attendant and drew near at the emperor's left and right.
idiomatic: He was later made Attendant and served close at the emperor's side.

literal: He followed the campaign against Murong Bao at Canhe.
idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Murong Bao at Canhe.

literal: At the beginning of Huangshi he was appointed Colonel of Valiant Cavalry and managed the night guards and forbidden brigades.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangshi he was made Colonel of Valiant Cavalry and managed the night guards and forbidden brigades.

literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, bandits rose together in Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu commanderies; Jin, with Lueyang's Xi Yuanzun and others, pacified them.
idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, bandits rose in Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu; Jin, with Xi Yuanzun of Lueyang and others, suppressed them.

literal: He followed campaigns and broke the Gaoche tribes.
idiomatic: He followed campaigns and broke the Gaoche tribes.

literal: He again broke the Kudi and Youlian tribes and moved their separate tribal settlements south of the passes.
idiomatic: He again broke the Kudi and Youlian tribes and moved their separate settlements south of the passes.

literal: He advanced again against the Houmochen tribe, reached Da'e Valley, set a garrison, and returned.
idiomatic: He advanced again against the Houmochen, reached Da'e Valley, set a garrison, and withdrew.

literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Imperial Waterways, went out as General of Jin Troops and Inspector of Youzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyang.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Imperial Waterways, sent out as General of Jin Troops and Inspector of Youzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyang.

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, he was General of Zheng Troops.
idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, he was General of Zheng Troops.

literal: An edict said that because Jin's family for generations had been loyal and filial, his father Dan was posthumously given Marquis of Changning.
idiomatic: An edict noted that Jin's family had been loyal and filial for generations and posthumously enfeoffed his father Dan as Marquis of Changning.

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan visited Yunzhong, Jin remained to guard the capital.
idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan visited Yunzhong, Jin remained to guard the capital.

literal: Prince of Changli Murong Bo'er plotted rebellion; Jin summoned him into the eastern wing of Tian'an Hall and executed him.
idiomatic: Prince of Changli Murong Bo'er plotted rebellion; Jin summoned him to the eastern wing of Tian'an Hall and executed him.

literal: An edict ordered him, with Duke of Nanping Changsun Song and others, to sit together in the Hall of Audience and record and decide on prisoners.
idiomatic: An edict ordered him, with Duke of Nanping Changsun Song and others, to sit in the Hall of Audience and decide criminal cases.

literal: Emperor Mingyuan held a great review at the eastern suburb.
idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan held a great military review at the eastern suburb.

literal: In martial exercises Jin acted as Left Chancellor; a great hunt was held at Mount Shihui.
idiomatic: At the martial exercises Jin acted as Left Chancellor; a great hunt was held at Mount Shihui.

literal: When the imperial carriage toured the west, an edict ordered Jin to go ahead as vanguard and attack the Yuele tribe at Mount Lu'na, routing them greatly.
idiomatic: On the western tour an edict ordered Jin ahead as vanguard to attack the Yuele at Mount Lu'na, routing them decisively.

literal: Another edict ordered Jin, with Changsun Song and eight others, to sit to the left of the stopping chariot gate and hear and decide the myriad affairs.
idiomatic: Another edict seated Jin with Changsun Song and eight others to the left of the stopping-chariot gate to hear and decide the myriad affairs of state.

literal: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and his rank advanced to duke.
idiomatic: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and advanced to duke.

literal: He was ordered to enter and leave in a light carriage with full guard of honor and attendants.
idiomatic: He was ordered to enter and leave in a light carriage with full guard and attendants.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu was crown prince and held court to hear government, Jin was made Left Assistant.
idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu was crown prince and held court, Jin was made Left Assistant.

literal: When the deposed ruler of Song Yifu was established, his state was inwardly divided and obstructed.
idiomatic: When Song's deposed ruler Yifu was restored, that realm was inwardly divided and obstructed.

literal: Thereupon Jin was sent to recover the lands south of the Yellow River; he was given credentials, overall command of vanguard military affairs, Minister of Works, Grand General of Jin Troops, and acting Inspector of Yangzhou.
idiomatic: Jin was then sent to recover lands south of the Yellow River with credentials, overall command of the vanguard, the post of Minister of Works, Grand General of Jin Troops, and acting Inspector of Yangzhou.

literal: He led General of Wu Troops Gongsun Biao and others south.
idiomatic: He led General of Wu Troops Gongsun Biao and others south.

literal: Using Biao's plan he attacked Huatai but could not take it and requested reinforcements.
idiomatic: Following Biao's plan he attacked Huatai but could not take it and requested reinforcements.

literal: The emperor was angry that he had not first seized territory and sharply reproached him.
idiomatic: The emperor, angry that he had not first seized territory, sharply reproached him.

literal: He then personally toured south, halting at Zhongshan; Jin from Huatai pressed toward Luoyang, driving hard to Wulao, and thereupon pacified Yan and Yu commanderies.
idiomatic: He then toured south in person, halting at Zhongshan; Jin pressed from Huatai toward Luoyang, driving hard to Wulao, and pacified Yan and Yu commanderies.

literal: He returned to besiege Wulao.
idiomatic: He returned to besiege Wulao.

literal: When Wulao fell, Jin set garrison officials to pacify it.
idiomatic: When Wulao fell, Jin set garrison officials to pacify the region.

literal: From the beginning of Wei, when great generals marched, only Changsun Song resisted Song Wu; when Jin campaigned in Henan he alone was given water clocks and the twelve yak-tail banners.
idiomatic: Since the founding of Wei, when great generals took the field only Changsun Song had resisted Song Wu; when Jin campaigned in Henan he alone received water clocks and the twelve yak-tail banners.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, his rank was advanced to Prince of Yicheng and he still held Minister of Works.
idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, Jin was advanced to Prince of Yicheng while retaining Minister of Works.

literal: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned against Helian Chang he sent Jin to lead General of Righteous Troops Feng Li and others in a surprise attack on Puban.
idiomatic: Campaigning against Helian Chang, the emperor sent Jin to lead General of Righteous Troops Feng Li and others in a surprise attack on Puban.

literal: Jin again held the Long Wall in the west; the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all came to submit.
idiomatic: Jin again held the Long Wall in the west, and the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all submitted.

literal: Jin stood in stalemate with Helian Ding, repeatedly fighting and breaking Ding.
idiomatic: Jin stood in stalemate with Helian Ding, repeatedly fighting and defeating him.

literal: When Ding heard that Chang had been defeated, he fled up to Shanggui.
idiomatic: When Ding heard Chang had been defeated, he fled to Shanggui.

literal: Jin pursued to Yong but could not overtake him and returned.
idiomatic: Jin pursued to Yong but could not overtake him and withdrew.

literal: An edict ordered Jin to withdraw the army; Jin asked to take advantage of their peril to pacify them and advanced to attack Anding.
idiomatic: An edict ordered withdrawal; Jin asked to exploit their peril and pacify them, and advanced on Anding.

literal: Chang retreated to defend Pingliang; Jin encamped at Anding, and because grain was exhausted and horses died, he deeply fortified and held firm.
idiomatic: Chang retreated to defend Pingliang; Jin encamped at Anding; when grain ran out and horses died, he fortified deeply and held firm.

literal: Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Gu attacked Chang and captured him.
idiomatic: Supervising Army Attendant Censor An Gu attacked Chang and captured him.

literal: Chang's troops again made Chang's younger brother Ding master and defended Pingliang.
idiomatic: Chang's troops then made his younger brother Ding master and defended Pingliang.

literal: Jin was ashamed that as commander-in-chief the merit of capturing Chang was not his; he abandoned baggage and pursued Ding at Pingliang.
idiomatic: Jin was ashamed that as commander-in-chief the capture of Chang was not his merit; he abandoned baggage and pursued Ding at Pingliang.

literal: Ding's troops were about to sally forth when a minor officer guilty of a fault fled into the enemy and fully reported the truth.
idiomatic: Ding's troops were about to sally when a minor officer guilty of a fault fled to the enemy and told all.

literal: Ding knew Jin's army lacked grain and water and thereupon intercepted Jin front and rear.
idiomatic: Learning that Jin's army lacked grain and water, Ding intercepted him front and rear.
